title: Dasakam 53 — Dhenukāsuravadha
description: Krishna begins tending the cattle, enters the Tāla forest with Balarama, and watches as Dhenuka and his attendants are cast from the trees; the boys enjoy the fruits and return home praised by the people of Vraja.
translation_note: No vetted stanza translation supplied. Numbered Facebook captions are preserved verbatim as commentary; the two unnumbered pictures do not provide a stanza-specific scene and are not assigned.

stanzas.sanskrit:
अतीत्य बाल्यं जगतां पते त्व-
-मुपेत्य पौगण्डवयो मनोज्ञम् ।
उपेक्ष्य वत्सावनमुत्सवेन
प्रावर्तथा गोगणपालनायाम् ॥ ५३-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
atītya bālyaṃ jagatāṃ pate tva-
-mupetya paugaṇḍavayo manojñam |
upekṣya vatsāvanamutsavena
prāvartathā gogaṇapālanāyām || 53-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna passed his childhood age and attained the charming age of boyhood which is between 6 to 10 years. Krishna gave up tending of the calves and enthusiastically started herding cows and cattle.

stanzas.sanskrit:
उपक्रमस्यानुगुणैव सेयं
मरुत्पुराधीश तव प्रवृत्तिः ।
गोत्रापरित्राणकृतेऽवतीर्ण-
-स्तदेव देवाऽऽरभथास्तदा यत् ॥ ५३-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
upakramasyānuguṇaiva seyaṃ
marutpurādhīśa tava pravṛttiḥ |
gotrāparitrāṇakṛte’vatīrṇa-
-stadeva devā”rabhathāstadā yat || 53-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna's reason to incarnate was to protect Gothra, the earth and cows. As first step, Krishna started to protect cows, befitting the reason he took to incarnate.

stanzas.sanskrit:
कदापि रामेण समं वनान्ते
वनश्रियं वीक्ष्य चरन् सुखेन ।
श्रीदामनाम्नः स्वसखस्य वाचा
मोदादगा धेनुककाननं त्वम् ॥ ५३-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kadāpi rāmeṇa samaṃ vanānte
vanaśriyaṃ vīkṣya caran sukhena |
śrīdāmanāmnaḥ svasakhasya vācā
modādagā dhenukakānanaṃ tvam || 53-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna and his brother Balarama were happily roaming about admiring the beauty of the forest. On friend Sudaamaa's suggestion, both of them excitingly entered the Dhenuka forest.

stanzas.sanskrit:
उत्तालतालीनिवहे त्वदुक्त्या
बलेन धूतेऽथ बलेन दोर्भ्याम् ।
मृदुः खरश्चाभ्यपतत्पुरस्तात्
फलोत्करो धेनुकदानवोऽपि ॥ ५३-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
uttālatālīnivahe tvaduktyā
balena dhūte’tha balena dorbhyām |
mṛduḥ kharaścābhyapatatpurastāt
phalotkaro dhenukadānavo’pi || 53-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Balarama shook the long Jambu trees in the forest. A bunch of ripe and unripe fruits began to fall. Along with the fruit, the demon Denukasura appeared in the form of a donkey.

stanzas.sanskrit:
समुद्यतो धैनुकपालनेऽहं
कथं वधं धैनुकमद्य कुर्वे ।
इतीव मत्वा ध्रुवमग्रजेन
सुरौघयोद्धारमजीघनस्त्वम् ॥ ५३-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
samudyato dhainukapālane’haṃ
kathaṃ vadhaṃ dhainukamadya kurve |
itīva matvā dhruvamagrajena
suraughayoddhāramajīghanastvam || 53-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Dhenuka means cow, Krishna being the protector of cows did not want to kill the asura with the cow name. So Krishna made his brother Balarama to kill Dhenukasura.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तदीयभृत्यानपि जम्बुकत्वे-
-नोपागतानग्रजसम्युतस्त्वम् ।
जम्बूफलानीव तदा निरास्थ-
-स्तालेषु खेलन् भगवन् निरास्थः ॥ ५३-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tadīyabhṛtyānapi jambukatve-
-nopāgatānagrajasamyutastvam |
jambūphalānīva tadā nirāstha-
-stāleṣu khelan bhagavan nirāsthaḥ || 53-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Dhenukasura's friends came rushing in the form of jackals and attacked the brothers. But Krishna and Balarama effortlessly threw them as if they were jambu fruits.

stanzas.sanskrit:
विनिघ्नति त्वय्यथ जम्बुकौघं
सनामकत्वाद्वरुणस्तदानीम् ।
भयाकुलो जम्बुकनामधेयं
श्रुतिप्रसिद्धं व्यधितेति मन्ये ॥ ५३-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vinighnati tvayyatha jambukaughaṃ
sanāmakatvādvaruṇastadānīm |
bhayākulo jambukanāmadheyaṃ
śrutiprasiddhaṃ vyadhiteti manye || 53-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Lord Varuna who witnessed the event was shocked as he too had a name called Jambuka and was scared to reveal it outside for the fear that he would be in danger too. It is for this reason that Varuna's name as 'Jambuka' is not known.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तवावतारस्य फलं मुरारे
सञ्जातमद्येति सुरैर्नुतस्त्वम् ।
सत्यं फलं जातमिहेति हासी
बालैः समं तालफलान्यभुङ्क्थाः ॥ ५३-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tavāvatārasya phalaṃ murāre
sañjātamadyeti surairnutastvam |
satyaṃ phalaṃ jātamiheti hāsī
bālaiḥ samaṃ tālaphalānyabhuṅkthāḥ || 53-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Devas who witnessed the killing of Denuka, praised Bhagwan that the fruit of incarnation has now appeared. Krishna laughingly said that He got the fruits in Denukavanam now and saying so ate the fruits.

stanzas.sanskrit:
मधुद्रवस्रुन्ति बृहन्ति तानि
फलानि मेदोभरभृन्ति भुक्त्वा ।
तृप्तैश्च दृप्तैर्भवनं फलौघं
वहद्भिरागाः खलु बालकैस्त्वम् ॥ ५३-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
madhudravasrunti bṛhanti tāni
phalāni medobharabhṛnti bhuktvā |
tṛptaiśca dṛptairbhavanaṃ phalaughaṃ
vahadbhirāgāḥ khalu bālakaiṣṭvam || 53-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Krishna and Gopa boys ate the honey dripping juicy fruits to their heart content.
They carried loads of fruits to their houses in the evening.

stanzas.sanskrit:
हतो हतो धेनुक इत्युपेत्य
फलान्यदद्भिर्मधुराणि लोकैः ।
जयेति जीवेति नुतो विभो त्वं
मरुत्पुराधीश्वर पाहि रोगात् ॥ ५३-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hato hato dhenuka ityupetya
phalānyadadbhirmadhurāṇi lokaiḥ |
jayeti jīviti nuto vibho tvaṃ
marutpurādhīśvara pāhi rogāt || 53-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
The people at Vrindavana welcomed the boys and happy over Denukasura vadham, praised the brothers for their mighty valour and ate the sweet fruits happily.

Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan to cure him of his afflictions.
